newsitem.title: USA: IBP '96 earnings hurt by exports decline.
newsitem.headline: IBP '96 earnings hurt by exports decline.

text.p: IBP Inc attributed its lower 1996 sales and earnings to a falloff in exports and plant startup expenses.

"Changing livestock supplies, an unexpected decline in exports and plant start up expenses contributed to tough comparisons in the second half of the year," said chairman Robert Peterson in a statement.
Tight hog supplies, coupled with a substantial expansion of the nation's pork processing capacity, continue to hurt the profitability of IBP's pork operations, the company said.

For the first time in more than a decade, the company's international sales declined. Its 1996 net export sales totaled $1.7 billion, down eight percent from the record levels of 1995. However, 1996 export sales were still the second highest in company history. Exports represented 13.4 percent of the company's net sales.
Concerns about BSE -- also known as "mad cow" disease -- in Great Britain and an E. Coli outbreak in Japan resulted in a food safety scare among Japanese consumers.

Until hog numbers improve or production capacity declines, pork processing margins are expected to remain under pressure. Nonetheless, favorable global market dynamics, including strong consumer preference for pork protein and growing income levels among emerging nations support the long-term attractiveness of pork, IBP said.

This week the meat company began beef processing operations at its newly expanded beef operation in Alberta, Canada. The plant, which became part of IBP when the company purchased Lakeside Farm Industries in 1994, previously produced only carcass beef for sale to outside processors.

This significantly reduced U.S. and, consequently, IBP exports to the Far East, even though there has never been a case of BSE in the United States and the source of the E. Coli outbreak appears to be non-meat related.
Now that these concerns appear to be subsiding, red meat shipments to Japan have begun to return to more normal levels, IBP said.

For the fourth quarter, IBP posted earnings of $0.19 a share and for the year, $2.06. In 1995, it earned $0.36 a share in the quarter and $2.67 for the year, with both periods including a loss of $0.23 a share for early retirement of debt. Sales declined to $3.02 billion from $3.16 billion in the quarter and fell to $12.54 billion from $12.67 billion for the year.
